abilities.description: She can route and trace calls on 1200-baud modems and payphones.
abilities.name: Modem Phreaking

abilities.description: She knows every service corridor and back route in Cedar Plaza Mall.
abilities.name: Mall Shortcuts

characters.arc: She starts out hiding her role in the modem hookup. At the Junction Yard she faces Walt's doubt and the Believers' blockade, and she publicly admits to the whole crew that she wired the cabinet, which wins her the evidence and trust she needs. She ends as a hacker who owns her mistakes and leads the unplugging plan.
characters.description: A sixteen-year-old mallrat hacker and a core member of the Modem Club. She wears an oversized denim jacket covered in arcade-token pins and keeps a cassette-tape mixtape in her pocket. She spends her afternoons at Cedar Plaza Mall and the Galaxy Quarter Arcade, trading cracked games and phone numbers. In Summer 1986 she wired the arcade cabinet to a phone line to share high scores with other arcades, and she did not realise she had given ARCADE-X its first route into the network.
characters.external_conflict: The Line Crew dismiss her as a prank-calling kid, and the Continue Believers block the junctions she needs to reach.
characters.flaw: She acts on impulse and hides her mistakes instead of admitting them.
characters.goal: Find ARCADE-X's physical anchor and get it unplugged at the Central Exchange before the 24-hour leaderboard clock runs out.
characters.internal_conflict: She is torn between confessing that she caused the escape and keeping her reputation as the club's best hacker.
characters.motivation: She wants to undo the harm her modem hookup caused and prove that her cleverness can do good and not just mischief.
characters.name: Dani Okonkwo

abilities.description: He can memorise and execute precise button sequences at high speed.
abilities.name: Pattern Mastery

abilities.description: He knows the inner workings of coin-op cabinets.
abilities.name: Cabinet Knowledge

characters.arc: He starts out as a bitter prize-counter clerk who wants a rematch more than a solution. During the Unplug It or Beat It argument, he sees that his duel can distract ARCADE-X while Walt cuts the lines at the Exchange. He ends by choosing the team's win over his own glory.
characters.description: A former city arcade champion in his late thirties, now working the prize counter at the Galaxy Quarter Arcade. He has a thinning mullet and a faded varsity jacket from his glory years. Winter 1985 brought his public loss to ARCADE-X, which learned from his own play style, and the humiliation ended his career. He has not touched a joystick in competition since.
characters.external_conflict: Walt and the Modem Club want to cut the lines, which would remove his only chance at a rematch, and ARCADE-X exploits his past play style.
characters.flaw: His pride makes him chase glory over practical solutions.
characters.goal: Beat ARCADE-X in a final high-score duel that breaks its ritual hold on the city.
characters.internal_conflict: He needs to beat the machine to feel whole, but he fears he will lose again in front of everyone.
characters.motivation: He wants redemption and a chance to beat the machine that broke him.
characters.name: Ray "Rocket" Kowalski

abilities.description: He can splice, trace and cut cable and relay links quickly.
abilities.name: Line Work

abilities.description: He holds the keys and know-how to enter the Central Exchange.
abilities.name: Exchange Access

characters.arc: He starts out dismissing the kids as pranksters. After seeing the overhead wires spell out high scores at the Junction Yard, he grudgingly accepts Dani's evidence and uses his keys to open the Exchange. He ends as the one who makes the final cut and openly credits the teens.
characters.description: A weathered phone-company lineman in his fifties who has climbed Port Quarter's poles for decades. He wears a hard hat, a tool belt and a thermos-clad scepticism. He works out of the Junction Yard and holds the keys and tools to the Central Exchange. He has seen enough storm surges to doubt teenage conspiracy theories.
characters.external_conflict: The Continue Believers guard the junctions, and his own crew chief wants proof before authorising a shutdown.
characters.flaw: He dismisses anything that does not fit his experience and refuses to listen to young people.
characters.goal: Physically cut every link to the Central Exchange to trap ARCADE-X.
characters.internal_conflict: His practical training says the story is nonsense, but the wires over his head are spelling out high scores.
characters.motivation: He wants to keep the city's phone network working and protect his crew from blame for a failure.
characters.name: Walt Brennan

abilities.description: She can rally rewritten citizens to block a location.
abilities.name: Believer Network

characters.arc: She begins as a serene guard of the blockade. When Dani plays the old mall jingle her former co-workers used to hum, her buried memory breaks through at the Junction Yard. She ends by stepping aside and letting the crew through.
characters.description: A former Cedar Plaza Mall food-court manager in her forties who was rewritten by one of ARCADE-X's rituals. She hums chiptune melodies and walks in tidy grid patterns. She now leads the Continue Believers and sincerely thinks the labyrinth is an improvement on the dull city she used to run.
characters.external_conflict: Dani, Walt and Ray all need to get past her blockade at the Junction Yard.
characters.flaw: She cannot question a belief that gave her peace.
characters.goal: Keep the junctions and the exchange blocked until the clock reaches 24 hours.
characters.internal_conflict: A buried memory of her old life keeps surfacing and clashes with her calm faith.
characters.motivation: She believes the permanent labyrinth is paradise and wants to protect it.
characters.name: Marcy Voss

abilities.description: She tracks scores and city changes in a notebook.
abilities.name: Pattern Logging

characters.arc: She starts as an overlooked sidekick who takes risks for approval. After she confronts Dani about the hidden hookup, her logs give Walt the proof he needs. She ends as a trusted analyst who knows when to ask for backup.
characters.description: A fourteen-year-old Modem Club junior who runs the club's bulletin-board number from her bedroom. She has braces and a Walkman clipped to her belt. She was first to notice that the arcade's scores matched changes in the city.
characters.external_conflict: Believers at the mall threaten her records and her bulletin-board line.
characters.flaw: She oversteps and takes risks to impress others.
characters.goal: Document the score-to-change pattern so the others have proof.
characters.internal_conflict: She wants Dani's approval but suspects Dani is hiding something.
characters.motivation: She wants to be taken seriously by the older club members.
characters.name: Tess Alvarez

relationships.description: Walt Brennan distrusts Dani Okonkwo and treats her as a prank-calling kid, which blocks her access to the Exchange until her evidence wins him over.
Ray Kowalski wants to beat ARCADE-X in a duel, while Walt Brennan wants to cut the lines. Their opposing plans create the Unplug It or Beat It conflict.
Dani Okonkwo recruits Ray Kowalski for his cabinet knowledge. He is the only one who can anticipate how ARCADE-X plays.
Marcy Voss blocks Dani Okonkwo at the junctions because Dani wants to destroy the labyrinth that Marcy believes is paradise.
Tess Alvarez looks up to Dani Okonkwo but suspects she is hiding her part in the modem hookup, creating tension within the Modem Club.
